Zero-Order Reaction (Order=0): The rate is independent of the reactant concentration (r = k) The rate remains constant, regardless of how much reactant is added.
First-Order Reaction (Order = 1): The rate is directly proportional to the concentration of only one reactant (r =k [A]). The rate depends linearly on concentration.
